## Body

Plan 223 (per-seat capabilities, #183 A1 and A2) stopped at round 3 under ruling C33: the trust boundary is the user account, so pij builds no per-seat credentials. #183 was closed unmerged and A2 abandoned. The branch plan/223-a1-daemon on origin still holds round 2 (1fbe9476). Round 3 (fb9eda70) is local only, in worktree fleet-223-a1.

1. Spawn status race: STILL LIVE ON MAIN. Spawn's exit-status poll can read the status file after it is created but before it is written. The empty string fails to parse, and a child's exit becomes a 500 instead of a 502. Only Linux CI hit it. The fix is in 1fbe9476 (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs, status read: an empty status means "no exit yet", so return Ok(None); the spawn wrapper in crates/cli writes the status to a staged file and renames it into place). Its regression test is an_empty_spawn_status_is_not_yet_an_exit. Cherry-pick that part as its own small PR.

2. Owned post-commit work. If a store write is owned (it survives the caller being cancelled), then EVERYTHING that must follow its commit belongs in the same owned task: admission permits or slots, cache or in-memory map resyncs, in-memory retirements, success counters, events. Reviewers found five separate instances in one PR, each a cancelled HTTP/1 caller leaving the store and memory split. Before pushing, list every line after `.await` on the owned write and ask "what if the caller is dropped here?". Test it by pausing inside the admitted write, aborting the waiter, then asserting the post-commit state, with a positive control that the row committed.

3. Related review lessons:
- A cached snapshot install must be conditional: never install a read older than what the map holds. A per-key stamp, compared under the same lock the writers take, does it.
- A proof must be bound to what it acts on (carry the presented digest to the write), not cached as a boolean.
- A process walk must re-read a pid's start time after reading its parent and name, or pid reuse splices two processes together.
- Composite routes count in every operation class they exercise.

4. Receipt index habit (spoonbill asked for it after the fact). The mutation runner should, for each mutant:
- write a JSON spec (file, exact old text, new text; each must match once);
- record `git rev-parse HEAD` at the top of its log;
- restore byte for byte, then assert `git status --porcelain` is clean.
Then write an INDEX.md: mutant, finding, file:line at the final head, killing test, failing assertion, log, source SHA. If a mutant ran on an uncommitted tree, say which commit that tree became, and check mechanically (git show) that the mutated site and the killing assertion still exist at the final head. Multi-mutant batches are attributed by assertion: say so. Examples: session files a1r2-mut/INDEX.md and a1r3-mut/RECEIPTS.md.

5. Shared target etiquette (F145): sleep about 45s between back-to-back shared-build runs (waiters poll every 20s), or you starve the queue.

Leftovers, all abandoned and safe to delete: worktrees fleet-223-a1 (round 3, local commits) and fleet-223-mut (detached at 9a33e17), and branch coder/223-a2-clients (a27d1a6) in fleet-194-role-templates.
